A 40-year-old farmer presented to the emergency with complaints of abdominal cramps, vomiting,
diarrhoea and breathlessness. On examination there was drooling of saliva, constricted pupils, moist
skin and rapid pulse with slow volume. It was diagnosed as a case of organophosphate poisoning.
(a) Write down the pharmacotherapy for this patient.
(b) Write down the pharmacological basis of prescribed drugs.
(c) Why Oximes are not effective for carbamate poisoning?
(d) Enumerate other uses of antimuscarinic drugs.

(a) Pharmacotherapy of Status asthmatics
(b) Adverse effect and contraindications of beta blockers
(c) Kinetics of elimination
(d) Role of low dose aspirin for coronary artery disease
(e) Principles of bioethics

Explain why?
(a) Dopamine is preferred over Adrenaline for the treatment of cardiogenic shock.
(b) Volume of distribution of certain drugs exceeds total blood volume.
(c) Thrombolysis should be done as early as possible, within first few hours after myocardial infarction

A 58-year-old woman with hypertension and paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia
requires a calcium channel blocker that balances peripheral vasodilation with AV node
conduction slowing. Which benzothiazepine derivative is most appropriate?

A 32-year-old Caucasian woman experiences chest pain with exertion. She reports having
similar episodes in the past. It is determined that she is experiencing stable angina. She is
given nitro-glycerine to relax her vascular smooth musculature. Which best describes a
step on nitro-glycerine's mechanism of action?
Why is the onset of action of lidocaine delayed in infected tissue?
